title: Dunjunz, official flippy disc (Bug-Byte, 1987), Model B side
label: The game
notes: Dun1 and Coder, exported with oaknut-disc from the Model B side of HFE flux captures of the 1987 flippy disc made by VectorEyes for the beeb_hfe archive of original discs (catalogued as Bug Byte, Dunjunz, variant 1, with identical copies owned by pumpkin and ip) and passed to the project by the stardot user Pernod; the files are byte-identical to the NVG archive's Dunjunz.zip. Dun1 (&2000-&7FFF, the figures above) holds the whole game. Coder (&5000-&59AF, 2480 bytes, exec &5000; SHA-256 2809c2aca27673963f795033190d0668c59789161483f173b331a8b468ae1775) is run for every level: it reloads Dun1, loads the level, copies &3000-&473F down to &08C0-&1FFF and one of two images of &0400-&07FF (keyboard only, or with a joystick handler) into place, and starts the game. The game listing saves both files. The side holds three more programs, each disassembled on its own: Dunjunz (the title screen and loader, run as *DUNJUNZ), *EDITOR (Editor) and *DEFAULT (Default).

disassemblies.label: Dunjunz: title screen and loader
disassemblies.runtime: Dunjunz, load &26C0, exec &2700, &89C bytes. Run as *DUNJUNZ by the other side's BOOT once the disc is turned over, and again by the game after game over: sets up page &08 for Coder and the game, points the BREAK intercept at the game's next-level intercept, shows the title screen with its twinkling stars, then arms the intercept and runs Coder.

disassemblies.label: *EDITOR: level editor
disassemblies.runtime: Editor, load &1910, exec &239D, &158E bytes. The same level editor as the Master side's, using MOS 1.20's row offsets and reset entry: loads a level file (or starts an empty one), shows its map in MODE 2 to be edited with a cursor, and saves it with a wall block from Stones and its checksum balanced, encrypted as the game expects.

disassemblies.label: *DEFAULT: level restorer
disassemblies.runtime: Default, load and exec &1900, &4530 bytes. Asks for a level number and saves that level's original file, from the copies of levels 1-24 it carries, over LevelN on the disc in the drive, undoing the level editor's changes.
